# Draft:J&J Auto Wrecking

J&J Auto Wrecking is an automotive recycling and used auto parts business located in Marshallville, Ohio, United States. Founded in 1957, the company has operated as a family-owned business for multiple generations and specializes in dismantling vehicles and reselling reusable automotive components.
History
J&J Auto Wrecking was founded in 1957 by Joe Bebesi, Julia Bebesi, and their son, James Bebesi Sr., in Marshallville, Ohio.
Prior to starting the salvage yard, Joe Bebesi worked in farming and dairy operations. The idea to begin an auto wrecking business came from a friend in the automotive industry. Despite initial skepticism about operating a salvage yard in a rural area, the Bebesi family launched the business after determining they needed to diversify income sources.
In its early years, the company focused primarily on scrap metal recovery. According to reporting by The Daily Record, financial challenges during the late 1950s and early 1960s, including a recession and declining scrap metal prices, made operations difficult. The family borrowed money and sold farming equipment to sustain the business until scrap prices rebounded in the early 1960s.
Over time, J&J Auto Wrecking transitioned from primarily scrap metal processing to a parts-based sales model, with reusable automotive components becoming the primary source of revenue.
Growth and modernization
By 2006, the company maintained approximately 850 salvaged vehicles on its property.
In the 1990s and early 2000s, the business incorporated computer-based inventory systems and expanded its use of telecommunications and internet-based sourcing. James Bebesi Jr. introduced computerized cataloging and began purchasing salvage vehicles through online marketplaces, marking a modernization of the company’s operations.
Operations
J&J Auto Wrecking dismantles damaged or decommissioned vehicles and catalogs reusable components for resale. Parts include engines, transmissions, drivetrain components, body panels, and interior assemblies.
According to customers interviewed by The Daily Record, the company has maintained long-term relationships with regional body shops and repair facilities. Local business owners cited reliability and family management as key characteristics of the company.
Vehicles are typically dismantled and stored for parts for approximately one year, although some inventory may be sold more quickly depending on demand.
Ownership
As of the company’s 50th anniversary in 2006, ownership was held by James Bebesi Sr. and James Bebesi Jr., with founder Joe Bebesi continuing to work in the business into his late 80s.
